stages.name: Pattern Interrupt
stages.evidence: Opens with a bold stat: '40% of enterprise software spend is wasted on tools nobody uses.' Clear problem-first framing.
stages.gap: The disruption claim relies on a trend (AI consolidation) that every other deck is using. Not unique.
stages.question: Why is this the moment? What specifically changed in the last 12 months that makes this inevitable now?
stages.fix: Replace the generic AI trend hook with a specific, verifiable customer story from a named logo.

stages.name: Problem Belief
stages.evidence: Highlights $120B annual waste in SaaS sprawl with a Gartner cite. Shows workflow fragmentation pain via a 12-app screenshot.
stages.gap: No named customer quoted. Pain is described at category level, not buyer level. Who specifically loses their job over this?
stages.question: Can you name three specific buyers who told you this was a top-3 priority this quarter?
stages.fix: Add 2-3 verbatim customer quotes with name/title/company. Show churn data tied directly to the problem.

stages.name: Solution Credibility
stages.evidence: Product screenshot exists. Claims 'AI-native unification layer' with a live demo link.
stages.gap: No benchmark data. 'AI-native' is used 11 times in the deck — becomes noise. No explanation of what the model actually does.
stages.question: What specifically does the AI do that a simple API integration doesn't? Show me the before/after workflow.
stages.fix: Add one quantified proof point: 'Customers save X hours/week or reduce tool spend by Y%.' Kill the buzzwords.

stages.name: Founder Credibility
stages.evidence: CEO previously built and sold a SaaS integration tool (acquired by Salesforce 2019). CTO is ex-Stripe infra lead.
stages.gap: No mention of why this specific team builds this better than a Salesforce or HubSpot internal team.
stages.question: You sold your last company to Salesforce — why didn't you just build this inside Salesforce?
stages.fix: Add a 'Why Us' slide that explicitly connects each founder's background to an unfair advantage in this market.

stages.name: Market Upside
stages.evidence: Claims $45B TAM for enterprise software management tools.
stages.gap: TAM is top-down and sourced from a single 2021 IDC report. No bottom-up build. No explanation of how they capture any of it.
stages.question: Walk me through the bottom-up: how many customers at what ACV gets you to $1M ARR?
stages.fix: Replace the TAM slide with a bottoms-up model: ICP count x win rate x ACV = realistic $1M, $10M, $50M ARR path.

stages.name: Differentiation & Defensibility
stages.evidence: Claims 'proprietary integration fabric' and mentions 200+ pre-built connectors.
stages.gap: Zapier, Make, and Workato all have 5,000+ connectors. No moat articulated. No switching cost described.
stages.question: If Zapier launches an AI layer tomorrow, why doesn't your customer churn immediately?
stages.fix: Articulate the specific lock-in mechanism: workflow data flywheel, seat expansion economics, or compliance moat. Name it.

stages.name: Traction Validation
stages.evidence: 18 paying customers, $420K ARR, 140% NRR. Named two Fortune 500 logos in pipeline.
stages.gap: No cohort data. No churn rate. Pipeline logos are 'in evaluation' — not closed. ARR growth rate not shown.
stages.question: What's your monthly churn rate? Show me the last 6 months of ARR growth month-by-month.
stages.fix: Add a single slide: MoM ARR growth chart, gross/net churn, and CAC payback period. This is the most important slide in the deck.

stages.name: Risk Framing
stages.evidence: No risks section found in the deck.
stages.gap: Zero mention of competitive risk, technical debt, go-to-market risk, or burn rate. This reads as naive or evasive.
stages.question: What keeps you up at night? What's the scenario where this fails in 18 months?
stages.fix: Add a 'Risks & Mitigations' slide with 3-4 real risks and specific mitigation plans. Investors trust founders who name risk.

stages.name: Deal Logic
stages.evidence: Raising $4M Seed at $18M pre. 18-month runway. Use of funds broken out: 60% product, 30% GTM, 10% ops.
stages.gap: No milestone targets stated. '$4M gets us to Series A' — but what metrics define Series A readiness?
stages.question: What are the 3 specific metrics you'll hit by month 18 that make your Series A obvious?
stages.fix: Add milestone targets: '$4M gets us to $2M ARR, 50 customers, and 120% NRR — all Series A benchmarks for our space.'

stages.name: Personal Commitment
stages.evidence: Closing slide has a strong vision statement. Team is clearly passionate about the problem based on founder bios.
stages.gap: No personal financial commitment mentioned. No evidence founders have turned down other opportunities.
stages.question: What have you personally sacrificed to be here? Why this, why now, why you?
stages.fix: Close with a 30-second personal story that makes investors feel this team can't not build this company.

diagnosis.conviction_breaks_at: Stage 5 (Market Upside) — top-down TAM with no bottom-up undermines the 'fund-returnable' test. Stage 6 (Defensibility) compounds the doubt: no moat = no durable business.
diagnosis.biggest_red_flag: Zero risk acknowledgment in a competitive space. Reads as either naive or dishonest — both are disqualifying.
diagnosis.highest_leverage: Replace slide 6 with a defensibility slide that names the specific lock-in mechanism and backs it with data (workflow recreation hours, data portability limits, compliance certifications).
diagnosis.increase_p_invest: Add a bottom-up TAM model showing the path to $10M ARR, and explicitly name the switching cost mechanism that locks customers in.
